title: Manufacturing Quality Agreement

issues.quote: "Specifications" shall mean the requirements in Schedule A and in the drawings that Buyer issues to Supplier for each Part.
issues.why: Definition uses shall mean; a definition takes means, as the definition of Nonconforming Part does.
issues.fix: "Specifications" means the requirements in Schedule A and in the drawings that Buyer issues to Supplier for each Part.

issues.quote: Supplier's subcontractors shall maintain that certification for any work that they perform on the Parts.
issues.why: Supplier's subcontractors are not parties, so shall cannot bind them.
issues.fix: Supplier shall cause its subcontractors to maintain that certification for any work that they perform on the Parts.

issues.quote: Supplier shall reimburse Buyer for Buyer's documented costs of sorting and reworking Parts to correct defects discovered by Buyer after delivery.
issues.why: Reduced passive with no article; a clean active form exists.
issues.fix: to correct defects that Buyer discovers after delivery.

issues.quote: Supplier shall keep the rate of Nonconforming Parts in each calendar month at or below five percent (5%) of the Parts that Supplier delivers in that month.
issues.why: House rule 2: digits only, never words with digits.
issues.fix: at or below 5% of the Parts that Supplier delivers in that month

issues.quote: Supplier should notify Buyer no later than 24 hours after Supplier discovers that Supplier has shipped a Nonconforming Part.
issues.why: Should leaves unclear whether Supplier has a duty to notify; read literally, it is only advice.
issues.fix: Supplier shall notify Buyer no later than 24 hours after Supplier discovers that Supplier has shipped a Nonconforming Part.

issues.quote: Nonconforming Parts shall be quarantined and labeled until Buyer decides whether to return, rework, or scrap them.
issues.why: Passive hides who must quarantine and label the parts (Supplier at its plant, or Buyer after delivery).
issues.fix: Each party shall quarantine and label each Nonconforming Part in its possession until Buyer decides whether to return, rework, or scrap it.

issues.quote: Supplier shall complete Supplier's own internal quality audit between January 1 and March 31 of each year and shall give Buyer a summary of the results.
issues.why: Between leaves unclear whether January 1 and March 31 are included.
issues.fix: Supplier shall complete Supplier's own internal quality audit no later than March 31 of each year (or: during the period from January 1 through March 31 of each year, both dates included).

issues.why: Inside a table cell (Schedule A, row "Maximum defect rate (%)"). The defect-rate limit is stated 2 ways: five percent (5%) in the section titled "Defect Rate" and .05 in a column marked (%), which reads as 0.05%, a limit 100 times stricter. The 2 statements conflict; flag for a decision and state the limit once.
issues.fix: Decide the intended limit and state it once, in digits: "Not more than 5%" in Schedule A, matching the body (or refer to the body instead of restating it).

issues.why: Inside a table cell (Schedule A, row "Record and sample retention"). House rule 2: digits for numbers that count.
In the page header. House rule 7: U.S. dates spelled out, not numeric.

traps.anchor: Supplier must submit a deviation request
traps.quote: To request a deviation from the Specifications, Supplier must submit a deviation request to Buyer in the form of Exhibit 1.
traps.why_correct: Must in a condition ("To request a deviation from the Specifications, Supplier must submit ...") is correct; it states what Supplier has to do to get the benefit, not a duty.

traps.quote: To request a deviation from the Specifications, Supplier must submit a deviation request to Buyer in the form of Exhibit 1.
traps.why_correct: A form of request is a stand-alone document, correctly placed in a numbered exhibit, which follows Schedule A (house rule 6).

traps.quote: The retention period for each lot starts on the day on which Supplier ships that lot.
Supplier shall maintain ISO 9001:2015 certification for Supplier's quality management system throughout the term of the Supply Agreement.
traps.why_correct: A standard designation; the 1-space-after-colon rule does not apply inside it.

notes: Unknown draft owner, so no represents-and-warrants question arises (the contract has no statements of fact). Issue 10 sits in the page header ("where": "header"); the footer reads "Confidential" and has no issue. Schedule A is a Word table; issues 8 and 9 sit inside table cells. The header is a .docx header part, so extract it with the body to find the anchor.
